Timeline::fill_like¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signatures¶

Timeline Timeline::fill_like(int year, int month, int day) const
Timeline Timeline::fill_like(const std::string& date) const

Fill The Receiver’s Shape With One Local Date¶

fill_like() creates a new Timeline with exactly the receiver’s shape and timezone, then places the same local midnight in every element. The receiver is a geometry and timezone template only: none of its instants participate in the new values.

This differs from fill_nat(), which replaces only absent positions while retaining defined receiver values. fill_like() replaces the entire payload by construction.

Overloads¶

Call form

Accepted input

Interpretation

fill_like(year, month, day)

Three integer calendar fields

Validates the combined civil date.

fill_like(date)

YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY/MM/DD text

Parses a date-only token; surrounding ASCII whitespace is ignored.

Both overloads produce 00:00:00 in the receiver’s timezone. The timezone is not merely attached after constructing UTC midnight: local midnight is resolved to its proper UTC instant first. This distinction matters whenever local time has a nonzero UTC offset.

Example 1. A local [1, 2] template receives local midnight from integer fields, while preserving its shape and timezone.

const auto like = pluss::timeline::date({{"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"}})
                      .tz_convert("America/Edmonton");
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(like.fill_like(2035, 7, 8)) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[1, 2], tz=America/Edmonton)
[ 2035-07-08 00:00:00 2035-07-08 00:00:00 ]

Date-Text Forms¶

The text overload is intentionally date-only. A time, UTC suffix, or numeric offset would compete with the receiver’s timezone and undermine the promise of receiver-local midnight, so datetime text is rejected rather than truncated. Hyphen and slash separators are equivalent accepted spellings.

Example 2. Both date separators produce the same local date.

std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(like.fill_like("2036-03-04")) << '\n';
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(like.fill_like("2036/03/04")) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[1, 2], tz=America/Edmonton)
[ 2036-03-04 00:00:00 2036-03-04 00:00:00 ]
Timeline(shape=[1, 2], tz=America/Edmonton)
[ 2036-03-04 00:00:00 2036-03-04 00:00:00 ]

Scalar And Empty Geometry¶

Unlike the axis-0 structural operations, fill_like() never promotes a scalar. A scalar template produces a scalar. An empty template retains its complete empty shape; the requested date is still validated, but no payload elements are allocated.

Example 3. A valid leap-day fill remains scalar.

const auto scalar = pluss::timeline::date("2024-01-01");
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(scalar.fill_like(2040, 2, 29)) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[], tz=UTC)
2040-02-29 00:00:00

Example 4. Empty trailing geometry survives unchanged.

const auto cube = pluss::timeline::date({
    {{"2024-01-01", "2024-01-02"}},
    {{"2024-01-03", "2024-01-04"}},
});
std::cout << pluss::timeline::print(
    cube.empty_like().fill_like(2035, 7, 8)) << '\n';

Output¶

Timeline(shape=[0, 1, 2], tz=UTC)

Absence, Allocation, And Complexity¶

An absent instant in the receiver has no special status because receiver values are not consulted. It is replaced just like every other position. The result owns contiguous epoch-nanosecond storage and requires one write per output element, so time and payload storage are both linear in numel().

Validation And Failure Modes¶

The integer overload rejects invalid civil dates such as February 29 in a non-leap year, month 13, or day zero. The text overload rejects malformed text, datetime text, timezone-bearing text, and impossible dates. Timezone loading and local-midnight resolution also occur before the result is returned.

Example 5. An impossible date and a datetime token fail instead of being normalized or silently shortened to a date.

try {
  (void)like.fill_like(2023, 2, 29);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "rejected\n"; }
try {
  (void)like.fill_like("2036-03-04T12:00:00");
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "rejected\n"; }

Output¶

rejected
rejected
